To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

gene duplication has been a major source of the chemical diversity in plant secondary metabolism and that this diversity has played an important role in the evolution of plant defenses that co-opt insect digestive physiology.

gene duplication of threonine catabolism genes is a major source for the evolution of plant chemical diversity and that the duplicated threonine deamination pathway has evolved to function as a plant defense against herbivores.

1) a gene duplication event in tomato has generated a novel TD paralog (pTD2), 2) pTD2 functions as a defensive protein in plant defense, 3) the proteolytic activation of pTD2 is mediated by an insect protease, and 4) the crystal structure of pT2 provides evidence of adaptive evolution of pTD2 in the extreme environment of insect herbivore guts.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the evolution of chemical diversity in plants.
the role of gene duplication in the adaptive evolution of a novel chemical defense trait in higher plants.
understanding how plants have evolved to protect themselves from insect herbivores and the molecular basis of this defense.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
TD2 is a defensive gene that has been selected by the plant to reduce insect herbivory, which is achieved by a proteolysis-dependent mechanism that has evolved to be specific for insect herbivores.
gene duplication is a major evolutionary force that drives the adaptive evolution of novel plant chemical traits that mediate interactions with herbivores.

TD2 is the result of an ancient gene duplication that occurred prior to the divergence of Solanaceae, and that the duplication event has led to the evolution of a novel protein isoform with a specialized function in plant–herbovire interactions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the evolution of a defensive function in the duplicated TD2 paralog of Solanum species has been shaped by the selective pressures imposed by lepidopterous herbivores.
gene duplication of a key biosynthetic enzyme in plants has led to the evolution of novel defensive functions that target the herbivore gut.
gene duplication of threonine-deaminase (TD2) in tomato is an adaptive response to herbivory.
The main takeaway from our work is that
gene duplication is a major driver of plant defense against herbivores.
the evolution of plant defense against insects is not limited to the production of toxic secondary metabolites, but can also involve enzymes that degrade essential nutrients in the insect gut.
gene duplication is a powerful evolutionary mechanism for the generation of new traits that mediate plant–insect interactions.
